context.guidance: Record the destination of each outbound transfer of Personal Data, and check it against any restriction the Central Government has notified under §16(1). Rule 15 governs data made available to foreign States, and Rule 13(4) applies where a Significant Data Fiduciary is involved. Send any flow whose destination is not restricted to legal review, and state the destination in the notice.

value.fix: The default `aws_region = "eu-west-1"` means Personal Data goes to AWS Ireland (EU), outside India, unless someone overrides it. Treat this as an outbound transfer under DPDP §16. 1) Record it in the data-transfer register: destination country Ireland (AWS eu-west-1), the categories of Personal Data stored or processed there, the purpose, and the processor (AWS). 2) Check Ireland against the Central Government's current §16(1) notifications. If it is restricted, stop the deployment and move to an allowed region such as ap-south-1 (Mumbai). If it is not restricted, send the flow to legal review as the guidance requires, and have legal confirm any Rule 15 duties on data made available to foreign States and any Rule 13(4) duties if the Fiduciary is a Significant Data Fiduciary. 3) Stop the destination from being chosen silently: remove the default or set it to an approved in-country region, and add a `validation` block that only accepts regions on a legally approved allowlist, for example `validation { condition = contains(var.approved_regions, var.aws_region) error_message = "Region not approved for Personal Data transfer under DPDP §16(1)." }`. Any new region should then need legal sign-off. 4) Name the destination (Ireland / EU, AWS eu-west-1) in the privacy notice given to Data Principals, and update the notice whenever the region changes.
